chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'A man is not praised if he rises from the end of the night, prays his prayer in one go, and then one single unit/stroke, and then goes to sleep.'

key_terms.آخِرِ اللَّيْلِ: the end of the night (time for Tahajjud)
key_terms.ضَرْبَةً وَاحِدَةً: in one go / a single unit/stroke

ai.seo_question: What makes the night prayer praiseworthy according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques the superficiality of performing the night prayer (Tahajjud) merely as a ritualistic obligation to be completed and slept through, rather than as a profound spiritual engagement. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *khushu'* (humility and presence of heart) and the completeness (*kamal*) of worship, distinguishing between the physical act of standing and the spiritual reality of the prayer. It serves as a reminder that the merit of *Salat al-Layl* lies in its depth and devotion, not just its duration or timing.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukeyr who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘If a man were to stand at the end of the night, so he prays his Salāt in one go, and then he goes (away) and sleeps, is not Praiseworthy.’
en.sarwar: 21. Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from ibn Bukayr who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘A man who gets up in the end of the night to perform his nightly optional Salah (prayer), all of them at one time and goes away to sleep, is not very praiseworthy.”
